name: Eskenazi Museum of Art
funding: The art museum of Indiana University, a public university. Sidney and Lois Eskenazi gave $15M in 2016 for the renovation and the name.
watch: Indiana University cancelled the Samia Halaby retrospective in December 2023. PEN America urged reinstatement and a petition drew 8,000 signatures.
why_flagged: The art museum of Indiana University, a public university. Sidney and Lois Eskenazi gave $15M in 2016 for the renovation and the name.
records_note: It posts annual reviews for 2020 to 2023; parent Indiana University posts audited annual financial reports and names its nine trustees; no donor list online.
other_findings: Democracy Now!, 2024-01-17: Indiana University canceled Samia Halaby's first U.S. retrospective after three years of work, and that she was told her Gaza posts were the reason. The university cited concerns about the exhibit's integrity.

name: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts
funding: Campus Fund supporters (June 2026) in the top Leader tier: Bloomberg Philanthropies, Kenneth Griffin and Citadel, American Express, JPMorganChase, Hearst. David Koch pledged $100M in 2008 for the theater.
watch: Activists disrupted the Met Opera's Carmen on 21 November 2025, demanding Lincoln Center remove Koch names. Griffin was targeted at the Whitney, not here.
why_flagged: Campus Fund supporters (June 2026) in the top Leader tier: Bloomberg Philanthropies, Kenneth Griffin and Citadel, American Express, JPMorganChase, Hearst. David Koch pledged $100M in 2008 for the theater.
records_note: It posts Form 990 and audited statements, a named Campus Fund supporter list of June 2026, 67 directors, and archived annual reports to 2017.
other_findings: Democracy Now!, 2010-08-25: Democracy Now!, discussing Jane Mayer's New Yorker article, reported that David Koch funded modernization of Lincoln Center's New York State Theatre, which now bears his name. Guest Charles Lewis called Koch Industries “the Standard Oil of our time.” | WikiLeaks, 2010-08-23 (WikiLeaks header 2010-08-21): A New Yorker profile that Sidney Blumenthal forwarded to Hillary Clinton says David Koch gave $100 million in 2008 to modernise Lincoln Center's New York State Theatre, which now bears his name. It says the Kochs operate oil refineries and pipelines. (news item forwarded in a leak)

name: Kuindzhi Art Museum
funding: A Ukrainian city museum until 2022. Under Russian occupation it is run by the culture ministry of the so-called Donetsk People's Republic, which the US, EU and UK list as a sanctioned entity.
watch: Its Kuindzhi paintings were taken to a museum in Donetsk after the city fell in 2022.
why_flagged: A Ukrainian city museum until 2022. Under Russian occupation it is run by the culture ministry of the so-called Donetsk People's Republic, which the US, EU and UK list as a sanctioned entity.
records_note: The museum was destroyed in March 2022 and no official site, report, accounts, funder list or board turned up.
other_findings: Bellingcat, 2022-06-07: Bellingcat found the Kuindzhi Museum damaged but standing, with a sign placing it under the Donetsk People's Republic culture ministry. Mayor's adviser Petro Andryushchenko said its Kuindzhi paintings were handed to occupiers. The Moscow Times traced them to a Donetsk museum.

name: Mariupol Drama Theatre
funding: Rebuilt by Russian authorities and reopened on 28 December 2025 under the so-called Donetsk People's Republic, which the US, EU and UK list as a sanctioned entity.
watch: A Russian airstrike hit it on 16 March 2022 while civilians sheltered inside; AP counted close to 600 dead.
why_flagged: Rebuilt by Russian authorities and reopened on 28 December 2025 under the so-called Donetsk People's Republic, which the US, EU and UK list as a sanctioned entity.
records_note: The theatre was destroyed in March 2022 and reopened under Russian occupation; no official site, report, accounts, funder list or board turned up.
other_findings: Bellingcat, 2025-11-14: Bellingcat's report on Russia rebuilding Mariupol recalls the 16 March 2022 airstrike on the drama theatre where civilians sheltered; AP counted close to 600 dead. Russian authorities reopened the rebuilt theatre on 28 December 2025, with St Petersburg's governor present.

name: PinchukArtCentre
funding: Private centre founded in 2006 and run by the Victor Pinchuk Foundation. Pinchuk's fortune comes from Interpipe, a maker of steel pipes and railway wheels.
watch: In 2020 two PinchukArtPrize nominees withdrew with open letters after 28 guides were dismissed. The centre denies the sackings were over their union.
why_flagged: Private centre founded in 2006 by Victor Pinchuk, a project of his foundation. His fortune comes from Interpipe, a steel pipe and railway wheel maker. No sponsors listed.
records_note: No records of its own: its founder's Victor Pinchuk Foundation posts annual reports from 2009 to 2018; the centre lists staff, no funders or board.

name: Bienal de Artes Mediales de Santiago
funding: Chile's Ministry of Cultures, through its collaborating-organisations programme and audiovisual fund, plus donations under the Cultural Donations Law. 2025 partners: SURA, Nescafé, La Tercera, Radio 13c.
watch: Run since 1993 by the Corporación Chilena de Video y Artes Electrónicas. The 17th edition ran 9 to 26 October 2025, centred on the GAM.
records_note: Its organiser CChV posts annual reports for 2018 to 2025, yearly balance sheets, a statement of its two public funding programmes, and its directorate.

name: Circle Art Gallery
funding: Limited company owned by art collectors including Samit Gehlot (Intex Foundation), Tony Wainaina and Robert Devereux. It sells at international fairs and runs an annual East African art auction.
watch: Founded in 2012 under director Danda Jaroljmek. Built its first white-cube gallery in 2015 and joined Cromwell Place, London, in 2020.
records_note: The gallery's site posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board; its About page only names the art collectors who own shares.

name: Colección de Arte Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat
funding: Private museum run by the Fundación Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat, set up by the Loma Negra cement heiress.
watch: Opened October 2008 in a Rafael Viñoly building. A 2014 prosecutors' office report said Loma Negra, which the founder controlled, gained from the 1976 coup.
records_note: The collection publishes no annual reports, accounts, sponsor list or foundation board; its institutional page names only staff.

name: Museo Nacional de Artes Visuales
funding: Uruguayan state museum, a division of the Dirección Nacional de Cultura in the Ministry of Education and Culture.
watch: Created by Law 3,932 of 10 December 1911 as the Museo de Bellas Artes. Roxana Fabius has directed it since August 2025.
records_note: The museum has nothing of its own; its ministry posts annual memorias for 2010 to 2023, but no museum accounts, funder list or board.

name: Gallery 1957
funding: Commercial gallery founded in 2016 by British Lebanese construction owner Marwan Zakhem. Its Yaa Asantewaa Art Prize pays GHC 50,000 to the winner.
watch: Spaces in Accra and London. Zakhem's firm does oil and gas engineering and construction contracts and built the Kempinski hotel that houses the Accra gallery.
records_note: The private gallery's site posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board; the Yaa Asantewaa prize page credits one partner.

name: IZOLYATSIA
funding: Non-profit platform founded in 2010 in Donetsk. After 2014 most money came from unnamed international, EU and US grants. Creative Europe co-funds ZMINA with Trans Europe Halles and Malý Berlín.
watch: Russian-backed forces seized its Donetsk site in 2014 and run a prison there. It moved to Kyiv. Only 2011 and 2012 annual reports are posted.
records_note: IZOLYATSIA posts only 2011 and 2012 reports; it publishes no accounts, named funders or board.

name: Kharkiv Municipal Gallery
funding: Founded 1996 as Ukraine's first gallery with municipal status. The city council culture department decides on its premises.
watch: Upper halls closed since 2022 and its White Cube now serves the city's news studio. The ARTbasement, also a shelter, reopened in September 2023.
records_note: The gallery's site returned HTTP 403, so nothing could be checked; it is a city council institution.
